newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles' lover takes official charity role.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles' lover takes official charity role.

text.p: Camilla Parker Bowles, the woman whose love for future king Prince Charles led to the collapse of his marriage, took a step into the limelight on Monday when she became patron of a British charity.
The National Osteoporosis Society said that Parker Bowles, 48, had held the cause close to her heart since she lost both her mother and grandmother to the brittle bone disease.
Her new post increased speculation that her 20-year-long relationship with Charles may become more open after years of being cast by the media as wicked "other woman" in the ill-fated royal marriage.

Charles and Princess Diana divorced last July after both admitted adultery during their 15-year marriage. Diana publicly blamed some of the difficulties on Charles's love for Parker Bowles, who is herself now divorced.
Charles, 48, has been careful to avoid been seen in public with Parker Bowles but is keen to see her improve her image with the British people.
"It is excellent news that Camilla Parker Bowles has been chosen," said Iris Swain, a charity representative.
"I believe her new role will help us to alert more people to the fact that osteoporosis can happen to anyone and cause years of suffering and premature death."
Osteoporosis makes bones porous and weak and affects hundreds of men and thousands of women in Britain every year.
The charity said they it was still discussing Parker Bowles' first official engagement as patron.
